messages:
maria: Heads-up — found an edge case in the console: when you flip the new role-affinity toggle on a route, the UI shows the role as applied but the routing telemetry still attributes requests to the old rule.
alex: repro steps?
maria: create route -> enable role-affinity (team role = billing) -> save -> send traffic as service-account that has both billing + reader. UI shows affinity active but telemetry traces (per-route) show 'no-affinity' tag.
sam: could be a caching problem on the router or the attribution job runs async. Do we have a race when entitlements cache expires?
tanvi: is this only console-visible telemetry or does it affect actual routing (i.e., which model instance gets the request)?
maria: routing is correct — requests are routed to the right pool. This is only the telemetry/attribution label. But alerts and dashboards rely on the label so it's actionable bug.
julian: likely we update route config in control plane then router picks it up (fast), but attribution service reads role from token introspection which may be stale if token->roles cache hasn't been refreshed.
alex: two separate concerns: 1) UX consistency (console show vs telemetry) 2) accuracy of historical dashboards. For (2) can we backfill attribution once cache is refreshed?
sam: backfill is doable but expensive. Need to determine window length. If it's <5m we can accept some discrepancy.
tanvi: from UX side, we could add an interim banner: "Attribution may lag up to X minutes" while backend fix is in rollout. Better than confusing mismatch.
maria: +1 for banner. Also we should avoid exposing ambiguous states: maybe disable the role-affinity toggle until telemetry is consistent? that feels heavy-handed.
julian: agree with banner. On the infra side I'll add a small change: attribution service will check both live config and cached token roles and prefer live config when present. That should make labels match within one deployment.
alex: API semantics question — when console toggles role-affinity, are we emitting a config.version? We should attach a config_version to routes so telemetry can join by version rather than ambiguous timestamps.
sam: we do have a route_config_version field but it's optional. Make it mandatory on writes and have routers publish that in the request envelope. Then attribution service joins on route_config_version => deterministic.
tanvi: that schema change requires console + backend + router + attribution job updates. Rollout plan?
julian: propose feature-flagged rollout: backend accepts version field (default backfill to current v). Router will start publishing route_config_version in envelopes behind ff. Attribution service under ff will prefer join on version. Console shows banner until ff is enabled for tenant.
maria: Can UX show the effective version somewhere in the route details (small pill)? would help debugging.
tanvi: yes, but keep it subtle. "ver: 12" clickable to see diffs.
alex: telemetry sampling note — the attribution pipeline samples traces for high QPS routes. If we add version joins, we must include version in sampled export keys to avoid extra cardinality explosion. Ops concern.
julian: ops-bot FYI: increased cardinality risk if we add version dimension. We should TTL versions and only keep last N versions per route.
ops-bot: alert: cardinality-growth-check scheduled for tomorrow at 03:00 UTC.
sam: OK, follow-up tasks: 1) make route_config_version required on route writes (backend PR) behind FF, 2) router change to publish version (router PR), 3) attribution join logic change (service PR), 4) console banner + version pill (frontend PR), 5) telemetry sampling tweak (observability PR).
maria: I'll open the UX PR for banner + pill and include copy: "Attribution labels may lag up to 5 minutes while routing metadata propagates."
tanvi: add a short QA checklist: impersonate service-account, change role-affinity, watch telemetry table, test both sampled and unsampled traces.
julian: I'll own the backend/router PRs, will coordinate with infra for safe deploy windows.
alex: I'll add an e2e test in staging that flips affinity and asserts telemetry label converges within <2m.
maria: Thanks — can we also add a small telemetry dashboard tile that shows 'route-config-version mismatch' count so we can monitor rollout regression?
sam: good idea. Observability person will love it.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: obs/metric-alerts/patch-39 -> staging (initiated by alex).
maria: perfect. Will track in the RBAC routing epic. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
